title_en: The Supplications of the Funeral Prayer
body_ar:
ما الدعاء الثابت في الصلاة على الميت وما صحة الدعاء الذي يسمى دعاء أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه؟

أن الدعاء في صلاة الجنائز ورد فيه كثير من الأحاديث، والدعاء الذي سأل عنه وهو الدعاء المنسوب إلى أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه موقوف، ثابت عن أبي هريرة لكنه لم يرفعه إلى النبي (ص)، أما الأحاديث المرفوعة عن النبي (ص) فمنها قوله (ص): (اللهم اغفر لحينا ولميتنا ولشاهدنا ولغائبنا ولكبيرنا ولصغيرنا ولذكرنا ولأنثانا إنك تعلم متقلبنا ومثوانا، اللهم من أحييته منها فأحيه على الإسلام ومن أمته منا فأمته على الإيمان، اللهم اغفر لهذا الميت وارحمه وعافه واعف عنه وأجره من فتنة القبر ومن عذاب القبر ومن عذاب النار، اللهم إن كان محسنا فزد في إحسانه، وإن كان مسيئا فتجاوز عنه سيئاته، اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله)، وغير ذلك من الأحاديث التي في معنى هذا (اللهم إن صاحبنا قد نزل بك وأنت أكرم منزول به، اللهم فأكرم نزله ووسع مدخله وأبدله دارا خيرا من داره وأهلا خيرا من أهله وزوجا خيرا من زوجه واغسله بالماء والثلج والبرد ونقه من الخطايا كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض من الدنس)، إلى غير ذلك من الأحاديث.
body_en:
What is the supplication that is established in the prayer over the dead, and what is the soundness of the supplication called the supplication of Abu Hurayra, God be pleased with him?

Many reports have come down concerning supplication in the funeral prayer. The supplication he asked about — the one ascribed to Abu Hurayra, God be pleased with him — is a report stopping at a Companion (mawqūf): it is established from Abu Hurayra, but he did not trace it back to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. As for the reports traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ), among them are his words, peace and blessings be upon him: 'O God, forgive our living and our dead, our present and our absent, our elder and our younger, our male and our female. You know our comings and goings and our resting place. O God, whomever of us You keep alive, keep him alive upon Islam; and whomever of us You cause to die, cause him to die upon faith. O God, forgive this dead person and have mercy on him, and grant him well-being and pardon him, and shelter him from the trial of the grave and from the punishment of the grave and from the punishment of the Fire. O God, if he was a doer of good, then increase him in his good; and if he was a wrongdoer, then overlook his misdeeds. O God, do not deprive us of his reward and do not put us to trial after him, and forgive us and forgive him.' And there are others besides that among the reports carrying this same sense: 'O God, our companion has alighted with You, and You are the most generous with whom any guest alights. O God, so make his lodging generous, and widen his place of entry, and give him in exchange a home better than his home, and a family better than his family, and a spouse better than his spouse; and wash him with water and snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt.' And there are still others besides these among the reports.

flags.arabic: اللهم من أحييته منها فأحيه على الإسلام ومن أمته منا
options: read منها as a slip for منا and render 'whomever of us', flagging the defect
leave the clause untranslated as corrupt
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The first of the two parallel clauses reads منها ('of it') where the second, identical in structure, reads منا ('of us'). The attested wording of this supplication has minnā in both. This is a transcription slip. The defective spelling is preserved in body_ar per the house rule; the English gives the evident reading. This matters more than an ordinary typo because the text is a recited formula: anyone reciting from body_ar would be reciting the slip.

flags.context: the Sheikh's grading of the supplication ascribed to Abu Hurayra
options: a report stopping at a Companion (mawqūf) / traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ)
a halted report / an elevated report
flags.note: These are the Sheikh's own technical gradings and they are the substance of his answer, so they must not be flattened. He says the Abu Hurayra supplication is established (thābit) from Abu Hurayra but mawqūf — Abu Hurayra did not trace it to the Prophet. He does not say it is weak, and he does not say it may not be used; he answers the question of its grading and no more. The English must not be read as a ruling against using it, and nothing to that effect has been added.

options: and You are the most generous with whom any guest alights
and You are the most generous of hosts
and You are the noblest with whom one can alight
flags.note: The Arabic is a passive participle construction with no natural English equivalent: 'the most generous one alighted upon'. Option 2 reads more naturally but imports 'host', which is not the figure — the figure is the traveller arriving at a dwelling, which is why the next clause asks that his 'lodging' be made generous. The more awkward rendering has been kept so that the image survives into the following clauses.

Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-23 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
Both supplications are recited formulae, so the Arabic in body_ar is the operative text and the English is given for meaning only.
The Sheikh names no collection for either supplication and gives no grading beyond mawqūf and marfūʿ; nothing has been supplied.
'Soundness' in the question renders ṣiḥḥah, the questioner's word, which is asking after the hadith grading rather than after validity in the legal sense.
